answer: Because the oasis index resolves every citation against the river checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the umber audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 94 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 94 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 14 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
